editorial.headline: A Clear Route for Driver-Provided Passenger Hire
editorial.standfirst: For charter, excursions and door-to-door driver-provided hire, this activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership and remains available for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
Rental Passenger Transport covers door-to-door passenger journeys in public passenger cars where the fare is agreed between the user and the transport provider. Its centre of gravity is the arranged trip: charter work, excursions and other seasonal charter transport are expressly within scope. The category also includes the hire of cars or other private vehicles with a driver, whether arranged through an app or not, as well as driver-provided hire using vehicles such as bajaj, kancil and bentor.

The agreed fare is part of the definition, as is the provision of a driver. This is therefore a category built around passenger movement on terms settled between provider and user, rather than around one particular booking channel or vehicle type. Registration is open at the Micro, Small, Medium and Large scales. The stated scope carries the same central idea across those scales: passenger transportation with a driver, encompassing door-to-door journeys, charter and excursion work, and app-based or non-app-based vehicle hire.

Nationally, foreign investment is open, and the stated foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. Put plainly, foreign ownership is not capped below full ownership at the national level for this activity. That position is recorded under Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Bali’s position is also materially clear: the record marks the activity as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and does not block PMA registration. At the Large scale, the OSS risk is Medium-High/High, placing it outside Bali’s permanent, island-wide moratorium on Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA.

Accordingly, a foreign investor can register this activity in Bali today. That conclusion is precise rather than expansive: Bali’s moratorium remains permanent and island-wide for PMA in the Low and Medium-Low risk categories, while this record identifies Medium-High/High OSS risk at the Large scale and expressly says it is not blocked by that moratorium. For founders, the essential reading is straightforward: this is an open national activity with a Bali position that remains available on the record presented.
